newsitem.title: USA: Drug works in some cases of kidney disease-study.
newsitem.headline: Drug works in some cases of kidney disease-study.

text.p: A hormone-like drug that is supposed to improve the function of the kidneys works only when the amount of urine coming from the kidney is reduced, according to a study in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine.
The drug anaritide, also known by the brand name Auriculin, was given to critically ill people with acute tubular necrosis, which is a severe form of kidney damage.

A group led by two researchers from Scios Inc., which makes Auriculin, found that, as a general rule, the drug did not work and people who got it were no more likely to survive without dialysis than volunteers who got a placebo.

The exception was in patients who were producing less than 400 milliliters of urine per day. In that case, the survival rate without dialysis was 27 percent in the anaritide group versus only 8 percent in the placebo group.

In an editorial in the Journal, Dr. David Humes of the University of Michigan Medical Center in Ann Arbor said: "The use of anaritide is a small step in our continuing attempts to improve the outcome of patients with this disorder."
